The minimum safe altitude the package's msaw.geojson surface has under this aircraft, in feet AMSL; 0 where it has none and 0 when the package ships no surface. The MSAW net measures the aircraft against this, and a label can show it, which TopSky cannot. Overlap is resolved as TopSky reads its file: the lowest order wins.

The controller-set manual alert on this aircraft, TopSky's four: 0 none, 1 missed approach, 2 inbound estimate, 3 irregular, 4 weather. With several standing, the lowest code; manualAlerts names them all. Set with the toggleManualAlert click actions and shared with every controller over the scratchpad (/MISAP/, /INBEST/, /IRREG/, /WX/, cleared by /MACLR/), so it travels with the flight; a package maps the code to its own words, usually on label line 0.

Every manual alert standing on this aircraft, space-joined in code order (missedApproach inboundEstimate irregular weather). Test one with ["contains", "manualAlerts", "weather"]; manualAlert reads only the lowest.

The controller's session, which a map item's showWhen reads and no aircraft, controller, METAR or frequency row does: myPosition (the position id the local login claims, empty with none claimed), onlinePositions (the other online controllers' position ids), arrivalRunways and departureRunways (every active runway as ICAO and runway, EGLL09L), aupAreas (the ids the vAcc's airspace use plan books for now, as the server relays it) activeAreas (the names of the datasets/areas.geojson areas active now), preActiveAreas (those a period opens for within their pre-active time), myCallsignEntry (the local callsign with each run of underscores made one, as TopSky compares callsigns; empty when not connected as ATC), onlineCallsigns (the other online controllers' callsigns, spelled the same way), coveredPositions (the position ids whose airspace the local login holds now, its own included, by the sector file's ownership order) and shownItems (the uuids of the automatic map items found shown so far in this pass; items are judged in file order and layers in manifest order, so an item reads only those before it). An area name is one entry, each run of whitespace an underscore. Each list is space-separated; read one with has or in.

An area list row, one area of datasets/areas.geojson as the client last judged it, which no other row reads: areaName, areaMapText (the label's text), areaCategory, areaState (0 inactive, 1 pre-active ahead of a period, 2 active), areaSource (0 none, 1 always, 2 a schedule, 3 the airspace use plan, 4 a condition with no times), areaAuto (1 when an entry activates it, 0 when only a hand could), areaStartDate, areaStartTime, areaEndDate and areaEndTime (the running or next period, UTC, yymmdd and HH:mm, empty with none known), areaLowerFt and areaUpperFt (feet, the period's else the area's, empty with none), areaUserText and areaAupId.

A net list row, one safety net of the active system as the board judges it now, which no other row reads: netName (the policy.json kind name: stca, msaw, apw, aiw, tct, ram, clam, bust, afdas, rimcas, emergency, ntz), netStatus (0 off by the system, 1 on, 2 hidden by safetyNets.show, 3 meant to run and cannot, 4 switched off by this controller), netMayOff and netMaySound (1 where safetyNets.kinds.(net).controllerMay grants off or sound), netSwitchedOff and netSoundOff (1 while this controller has switched the net or its sound off and the system grants it).

A plugin key: a tag item, written plugin:{plugin name}:TAG_{item name}, or an expression the plugin declares, written plugin:{plugin name}:EXP_{expression name}. As an itemName a tag item shows the plugin's value, or the item's default. As a condition key or an "&key" either reads what the plugin last pushed for the aircraft, else its default: a tag item's registered default, an expression's declared one. It reads empty while the plugin is not loaded and on a row that is no aircraft. A boolean expression reads "1" or "0".

[]: the condition that always holds, as an absent one does where absence applies.

items.description: The time zone the times are in: an IANA id such as Europe/London, or UTC.

from.description: The first day a window may start: MMDD for a period every year, YYMMDD for a single one.

to.description: The last day a window may start, in the same form as from. A yearly period may run over the new year.

days.description: The weekdays a window may start on, 1 Monday to 7 Sunday, or 0 to run from start on the first day to end on the last.

end.description: HH:MM, up to 24:00. At or before start, the window ends on the following day.

anyOf.description: A time window, TopSky's activation schedule: ["within", zone, {from, to, days, start, end}]. A window that passes midnight stays until its end on the following day.

items.description: The source line as the vAcc wrote it.

anyOf.description: ["unread", line]: a line neoradar-cli could not convert, kept so the author is told. It never holds, under a NOT too, and .dev package-check reports it as unreadable.

expression.description: One "$expression" reference, or an array of them. The rule matches when ANY referenced expression is true; a reference to an expression that is not defined is never true, and an empty array never matches. For conditions that must all hold, define one expression as ["AND", ["$a", "$b"]] and reference that alone.
